newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian consumer sentiment bullish - survey.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian consumer sentiment bullish - survey.

text.p: Malaysian consumers remain bullish about the economy, although concerns over inflationary remain high, a survey by the Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) found.

A survey of 1,248 households by the economic think tank in its third quarter report found that the financial situation of 22 percent of the respondents had improved while 64 percent said their situation had remained the same.
"Consumers appear to be still feeling very confident about the economy," MIER's quarterly report said.

"A stronger current financial position, more optimistic employment outlook and anticipated better financial position in the near future all contributed to an improvement in consumers' sentiment in the third quarter," it said.
But inflationary expectations remain high despite some signs of levelling off. "With spending plans firmly in place, such expectations may well turn out to be self-fulfilling," the report said.
Thirty-one percent of those surveyed said it was a good time to purchase major items, up from 28 percent in the second quarter and 29 percent in the third quarter of 1995.
But house buying intentions in the next six months appeared little changed from last quarter, when buying intentions were at their lowest level in two years, MIER said.
Nine percent said they planned a home purchase in the next six months against eight percent in the last quarter and 12 percent in the third quarter of 1995.

Spending plans for other consumer durables such as cars, furniture, television sets, washing machines and personal computers were sustained or increased slightly compared to the second quarter, but were noticeably lower than in the last quarter of 1995, MIER said.
Of those buying cars, 64 percent prefer a new vehicle while 36 percent would opt for a used car, it said.
